user.title: Exception Debug
user.description: Retain live traceback frames for recent Home Assistant exceptions so they can be inspected after the fact. All of these can be changed later from the integration's options.

data.enable_eval: Enable evaluating code in a captured frame

data_description.level: Only log records at or above this level are captured.
data_description.max_entries: Oldest exceptions are dropped once this many are retained.
data_description.ttl: How long a captured exception keeps its inspectable frames. Frames pin every local variable in scope, so a shorter value uses less memory. The text traceback is kept either way. Set to 0 to release frames immediately.
data_description.max_repr: Values longer than this are truncated before being returned.
data_description.enable_eval: Lets an authenticated caller run arbitrary Python inside a captured frame. This is remote code execution with full access to your Home Assistant instance — only enable it while actively debugging.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Only a single configuration is allowed.

deprecated_yaml.title: YAML configuration of Exception Debug is deprecated
deprecated_yaml.description:
Configuring Exception Debug in `configuration.yaml` is deprecated and your settings have been imported into the UI.

Remove the `exception_debug:` block from `configuration.yaml` and restart Home Assistant to resolve this issue. Settings can then be changed from Settings > Devices & services > Exception Debug > Configure.

not_configured.message: Exception Debug is not set up, so there is nothing to act on.
